newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Korea Exchange Bank plans Kangaroo bond.
newsitem.headline: Korea Exchange Bank plans Kangaroo bond.

text.p: Korea Exchange Bank plans to launch an Australian dollar-denominated "Kangaroo" bond in December, lead manager Bankers Trust Australia said Wednesday.
Kangaroo bonds are bonds issued by foreign borrowers into the Australian domestic market.

The fixed-rate bond issue is expected to be about A$180 million in size and will mature on December 15, 1999. Sales to investors will commence on December 10 and the settlement date will be shortly thereafter.
The bond will be priced to yield 37-40 basis points over Australian government bonds due in July 1999.

Both domestic and foreign investors can buy the issue, but Bankers Trust expects that the majority of the bonds will be sold into the local market. Roadshows were held in Sydney on November 25 and Melbourne on November 26.
The KEB issue is the second Kangaroo bond offered to Australian investors and the first to be launched following a change in government rules on foreign banks issuing securities in Australia.
Quasi-sovereign Korea Development Bank launched a A$150 million Kangaroo bond in August via lead manager Commonwealth Bank of Australia.

Speculation that the KDB bond opened the door for more Asian borrowers to tap into Australian savings came to a halt when it became clear that non-sovereign banks trying to issue bonds would run afoul of the law.

The law in question was Section 66 of the Banking Act of 1959, which prevented banks, unless licensed in Australia, from describing themselves as banks in Australia in relation to any financial business they might pursue.
Section 66 was designed to prevent confusion among retail banking customers about what constituted a prudentially supervised bank in Australia.
The law was relaxed in September to allow foreign banks to issue securities as "excluded issues" to investors in denominations of not less than A$500,000.
Bankers Trust said it expected most of the issue to be bought by institutional investors in lots of five, 10 or 20 million Australian dollars.
Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Macquarie Bank and National Australia Bank will also act as dealers for the issue.
